authoredFrom: PIN THE ABSENCE, 2026-10-17. bash's grammar has NO construction form and the analyzer has NO `instantiates` emission — case-insensitive search of src/ast/real-bash-analyzer.ts finds zero occurrences of the word, and parsing all 34 .sh/.bash fixture sources emits exactly calls/contains/exports/imports/overrides/references/uses. The constructs in this fixture LOOK like construction to a naive reader — an array literal, an associative array (`declare -A`), a command literally named `new`, a function used as a factory, and command substitution — and the forbid row pins that NONE of them produces an `instantiates` edge. WHY THIS FIXTURE EXISTS: script/m14/completeness-inventory.ts section-B reported bash as 'EMITTED but absent from requiredKinds: instantiates'. That reading is an INSTRUMENT ARTIFACT, not a bash edge: its emittedKinds() parses every non-JSON file in validation/m14/fixtures/bash, which holds 65 .ts/.mts helper modules alongside the 34 bash sources, and the TypeScript analyzer's `new WSP()`-shaped rows were attributed to this lane (43 instantiates edges, every one from a file whose detected language is typescript; zero from .sh/.bash). A fixture proving the absence is worth more than a pin on a fabricated kind; the correct fix is the inventory's file filter, proposed separately.

expectRelationships.note: a command whose NAME is `new` — the construct a naive reader mistakes for construction; bash publishes a CALL and must never publish instantiates.

forbidRelationships.note: THE WHOLE POINT: no construct in this file (array literal, declare -A, a command named `new`, a factory function, command substitution) is an instantiation, because bash has no construction form. The section-B 'bash EMITS instantiates' reading came from the TypeScript helper modules in this directory, not from this lane.
